reason: Diff and current head both verified directly: the Welcome nav anchor's guard was changed from `{{if and initWelcome isDeveloperAudience}}` to `{{if initWelcome}}`, dropping the audience check the checklist item correctness-25 requires (Welcome nav anchor hidden for non-developer audience). initWelcome in server.go is a static per-install flag (opts.InitWelcome, the --init-welcome flag) independent of audience, so any casual-audience install started with that flag now shows the Welcome/setup nav entry. The only test touching this path, TestWelcomeNavGatedByInitWelcome, never sets a casual audience, so the regression is uncaught — consistent with the candidate's own effect=incorrect, exposure=rare cells, which stand.
probe: none: tool-policy denies every executable form available in this worktree for a custom (non-repo-registry) verifier script on an HTML template — direct `bin/acdsl` (absolute and relative path) is denied with 'no allow rule matches', direct `bash <script>` is denied the same way, and the repo's Makefile has no `acdsl` target accepting ARGS (only `audit`/`build-audit`, neither parameterized) so `make -C <worktree> acdsl ARGS=...` has no target to call. Two distinct executable forms (bin/acdsl, bash script) were attempted and both denied, per the protocol's two-attempt cap before declaring unprobeable. Settled via the manual path instead: direct reads of the committed diff and the current head file, plus the Go source backing initWelcome/isDeveloperAudience and the one touching test.
